props.title: Narrow Margin
props.initialSlug: DA protects witness in deadly train cat-and-mouse game

sections.content: **Narrow Margin** (1990) reinvents the claustrophobic train thriller template established by The Lady Vanishes (1938) with muscular 90s action sensibilities. Gene Hackman's determined DA protecting Anne Archer while trapped on a Vancouver-bound train delivers tight, economical suspense that recalls the taut efficiency of the 1952 original **The Narrow Margin**. Director Peter Hyams shoots the train's confined spaces with a prowling camera that amplifies the tension, making the railway cars feel like closing trap doors.

sections.content: The train thriller subgenre hit its stride in the 1970s with films like **The Taking of Pelham One Two Three** (1974) and Silver Streak (1976) before evolving into the slicker action spectacles of the 1990s. Under Siege 2: Dark Territory (1995) and **Speed** (1994) amped up the pyrotechnics while maintaining the core appeal of heroes trapped in moving vehicles with determined killers. **Narrow Margin** bridges these eras, combining old-school suspense with modern production values.

Gene Hackman's performance anchors the film with the same kind of weathered authority he brought to **The French Connection** (1971) and **Night Moves** (1975). His cat-and-mouse game with James B. Sikking's ruthless assassin makes excellent use of the train's cramped corridors and precarious external walkways. The film's emphasis on practical stunts and real locations gives it a visceral edge missing from many contemporary green-screen spectacles. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Vehicle-Based Thrillers

sections.content: **Narrow Margin** sits at an interesting junction between the stripped-down thrills of **Duel** (1971) and the elaborate set-pieces of **Speed** (1994). Its focus on sustained tension over spectacular action sequences shows the influence of European thrillers like **The Last Express** (1976) and **La Femme Nikita** (1990), where confined spaces become pressure cookers for character dynamics.
